messages:
Nora (AM): opening CedarBank POC thread — they want Redwood Private in their AWS account, single stable egress IP for allowlisting, and completed security questionnaire. 8 business day POC.
Diego (SE): quick clarifiers: do they need original client IP preserved? and will corp TLS inspection be in path? Both affect design.
Kavita (NetOps): if they need stable egress IPs: provision NAT Gateway(s) with EIPs per AZ or use NLBs with EIPs. To preserve client IP to downstream, run serving inside their VPC behind NLB + proxy-protocol v2. PrivateLink is preferred over peering for cross-account stable endpoints.
Ibrahim (InfoSec): questionnaire phrasing suggestion: "No public inbound needed. Outbound: HTTPS (443) to control-plane FQDNs (*.redwood-inference.com) and model stores (s3.amazonaws.com). TLS 1.2+ enforced. For allowlist provide customer EIP(s) or use interface endpoints. Customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; KMS usage auditable via CloudTrail."
Diego (SE): small test they can run for PrivateLink:
```
curl -v https://vpce-0aa1bb.vpce-svc-zzz.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: api.redwood-inference.com'
```
Kavita (NetOps): note: VPC Peering may fail with overlapping CIDRs; recommend PrivateLink or Transit Gateway for complex topologies.
Nora (AM): action items: Diego -> diagram + curl test (today), Kavita -> firewall + NAT/EIP runbook (EOD), Ibrahim -> final questionnaire snippet (tomorrow). ops-bot: POC sandbox provisioned us-west-2 (build-1309). :rocket:
